instantiated_cells.justification: Legislative agents file expenditure statements with updated registration statements due the last day of January, May, and September (not annually).
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due tri-annually, not monthly.
Legislative agents must file expenditure statements with updated registration statements due the last day of January, May, and September—an 'other' (tri-annual) cadence.
The statute requires filing by the last day of January, May, and September, not quarterly.
A legislative agent must file expenditure statements tri-annually with updated registrations, not on a semi-annual schedule.
Updated registration statements (with required expenditure statements) are due three times per year—last day of January, May, and September—i.e., tri-annually.

cell.value: Last day of January, May, and September each year (tri-annual; 4-month reporting periods).

instantiated_cells.justification: The filing deadlines are fixed as the last day of January, May, and September, and each statement covers the preceding four-calendar-month period.

Legislative agents must disclose, for reportable expenditures, the recipient’s name, total amount, description, and approximate date (itemization by recipient and expenditure details beyond a lump sum).
A legislative agent files a statement of expenditures with each updated registration statement due the last day of January, May, and September (three times per year).
When reporting certain expenditures, the legislative agent must include the specific items of legislation (if any) for which the expenditures were made and the client identity.
Expenditure reporting excludes 'compensation paid to legislative agents' and there is no requirement for the legislative agent to disclose compensation received from the employer.
The bundled provisions require reporting expenditures and certain financial transactions but do not require reporting lobbying contacts.
For reportable expenditures, the legislative agent must report the specific items of legislation, linking expenditures to the issue/bill (if any) for which they were made.
The initial registration statement must include 'a brief description of the type of legislation' to which the engagement relates.
Legislative agents must report the type of legislation to which their engagement relates, which constitutes general-subject disclosure.
The definition of 'expenditure' includes gifts, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and §101.73 requires reporting of expenditures made to or for covered officials.

The statute defines employer-reportable expenditures to exclude office facility costs and compensation, and it does not require legislative agents to report non-compensation indirect lobbying costs as a separate component.

Legislative agents file expenditure statements itemizing recipient, amounts, description, dates, and legislation/client identity, and registration identifies the employer, but compensation paid/received is not required to be disclosed.
Registration requires the legislative agent’s name, business address, and occupation, but the statute does not require disclosure of a phone number.

The statute requires listing specific bills/resolutions lobbied in updated registration statements and (for certain expenditures) the specific items of legislation, but it does not require reporting the position taken on bills/actions.
The registration statement requires employer name/address (and real party in interest) but does not require stating whether the principal’s business is public or private or describing its nature.
The statute requires the employer’s business address but does not require disclosure of a phone number for principals.
Each legislative agent must register each engagement and disclose the employer (and any different real party in interest) by name.
Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.
Compensation paid to legislative agents is expressly excluded from 'expenditures' and thus is not a required reported component of the expenditure statement.
A legislative agent’s statement of expenditures must show the total amount of expenditures made by the legislative agent during the reporting period.

Lobbyists (legislative agents) must file their own expenditure statements with detailed itemization and identify their employer, but the statutes do not require them to disclose compensation received.
While legislative agents must file expenditure statements with updated registrations, the statute does not explicitly require a 'no activity' (zero expenditures) report when no spending occurred.
Reportable 'expenditures' are defined only as those made to or for the benefit of specified public officials/employees and their staff, not household members of those officials.

For certain expenditures (and meal expenditures over $50/year), legislative agents must itemize by recipient with total amount, description, and approximate date, rather than only reporting an aggregate lump sum.
